targetAudience.primary: Engineers and governance leads building agent runtimes that call effectful external tools
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands tool calls, authentication, human approval, retries, and external side effects.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A runtime may mistake evidence that explains an interruption—or a later approval that permits continuation—for proof that replaying the original call is safe.

whyNow: Two independent maintainer fixes in OpenAI Codex and Google ADK suppress autonomous reinvocation at authentication and human-confirmation boundaries, exposing a common recovery-safety invariant.

externalHook.description: Authentication challenges and confirmation pauses preserve information needed for recovery while deliberately stopping the current execution path from issuing another effectful attempt.

coreProposition: An interrupted tool call should preserve recovery evidence, execution authority, and effect evidence as separate state dimensions; a later authentication or approval event may restore authority but must not silently authorize replay while the prior external effect remains unknown.

originalValue.description: Separates recovery evidence, resume/execution authority, and external-effect evidence so that recovery cannot silently become replay authorization.

readerTakeaway: Model interruption as an evidence-bearing pause: retain occurrence identity and recovery metadata, then require fresh authority plus effect-state reconciliation before any replay.

supported: OpenAI Codex preserves MCP authentication challenges after bounded silent OAuth recovery fails and returns a failed tool-call result instead of replaying in that branch.
Google ADK prevents a confirmation-pause result from returning to the model loop and causing another tool invocation.
Both fixes support a bounded higher-order invariant that interruption evidence may survive while autonomous replay authority is withheld.
unsupported: A universal retry protocol for all tools
Proof of approver identity or approval scope
Proof that a remote side effect did not commit before an observed failure
uncertain: Which tool protocols can prove pre-effect rejection
How long approval remains fresh after arguments, credentials, or target state change
Which receipt schema best binds an external effect to a tool-call occurrence

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument compares general open-source agent-runtime mechanisms and does not depend on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The two implementation samples support a concrete cross-sample comparison, a bounded runtime-state model, and actionable engineering consequences without claiming universal validity.
